title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Beginning
full_review:
Depravity is once against packaged as entertainment in "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Beginning" (New Line).

A prequel to the 2003 horror film -- which was a remake of Tobe Hooper's 1974 cult hit -- the movie, set in 1969, revisits the homicidal Hewitt clan, who follow the bloody lead of their redneck patriarch, Sheriff Hoyt (R. Lee Ermey). The "beginning" in the title refers to Hoyt's hulking nephew, Thomas (Andrew Bryniarski), aka "Leatherface," whose early years as a chainsaw-wielding psycho are revealed in grisly detail.

Served up for slaughter this time is a foursome of road-trippers sidelined while driving across Texas: Vietnam re-enlister Eric (Matt Bomer), his draft-dodging younger brother, Dean (Taylor Handley), and their girlfriends, Chrissie (Jordana Brewster) and Bailey (Diora Baird).

Director Jonathan Liebesman forgoes plot to pile on the bloody sadism. Such gratuitous brutality isn't amusement, but something closer to pornography.

With any luck, this franchise finally ends with "The Beginning."

The film contains excessive gory violence, including graphic scenes of mutilation and dismemberment, a sexual situation, and much rough and crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
